questions.question: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant is called
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geitonogamy**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower is called pollination.

 
 
• Pollens are produced by the male part of a flower called the stamen.
 
• Pistil is the female part of a flower with stigma at its top.
 
• Geitonogamy is the process of pollination between two flowers of the same plant.
 
• The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant is called geitonogamy.
 
• Honeybee helps with the pollination of sunflowers.
 
• Bats help with the pollination in banana.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Autogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower.
 
• Xenogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a different plant, opposite the process of Geitonogamy.

questions.question: The correct sequence of parts of female reproductive organ in plants
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stigma, Style, Ovary and Thalamus**__.

__
 
• **Stigma **- It is the **head** of the pistil.

 
 
• It receives pollen, which begins the process of fertilization.
 
 
 
• **Style **- It the **stalk** of the pistil.
 
 
• It is a long, slender stalk that connects the stigma and the ovary. 
 
• When pollen reaches the stigma, it begins to grow a tube through the style called a pollen tube, which eventually reaches the ovary.
 
 
 
• **Ovary **- It is the **base** of the pistil.
 
 
• It holds the ovules for fertilization.
 
 
 
• **Thalamus **- It is present **near the stalk of the flower**.
 
 
• It supplies nutrients to the flower.
 
• It is a condensed axis of the flower from which all floral parts arise.

questions.question: Asexual reproduction takes place in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lower animals and plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** is a type of reproduction that does not involve the fusion of gametes (sexual cells) and results in offspring that are genetically identical to the parent organism.
 
• It is commonly observed in **lower animals and plants**, as they often have simple structures and mechanisms for reproduction.
 
• In **lower animals** such as hydra, sponges, and planarians, asexual reproduction occurs through methods like **budding, fragmentation, and regeneration.**
 
• In **plants**, asexual reproduction is widely seen in forms such as **vegetative propagation** (e.g., in potatoes, onions, and strawberries), **spore formation** (e.g., in mosses and ferns), and **budding** (e.g., in yeast).
 
• It allows for rapid population growth, particularly in favorable environmental conditions, as it does not require complex reproductive organs or processes.
 
• This form of reproduction is advantageous for organisms in stable environments where adaptation to change is not immediately necessary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plants**__

 __
 
• Plants primarily reproduce through both sexual and asexual methods, depending on the species and environmental conditions.
 
• Examples of asexual reproduction in plants include **vegetative propagation** (e.g., cuttings of rose plants) and **spore formation** (e.g., in mosses and ferns).
 
• Sexual reproduction in plants involves the formation of seeds through pollination and fertilization.
 
 
 
• **Higher animals**__
 __
 
• Higher animals, such as mammals, birds, and reptiles, reproduce sexually, involving the fusion of male and female gametes.
 
• Asexual reproduction is not observed in higher animals due to their complex biological systems and the need for genetic diversity.
 
 
 
• **Lower animals**__
 
 
• Lower animals like hydra, amoeba, and starfish exhibit asexual reproduction techniques like **binary fission**, **budding**, and **fragmentation**.
 
• These methods are simple and require less energy compared to sexual reproduction.

questions.question: Which of the following fruit develops through parthenocarpy?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parthenocarpy**

 
 
• Parthenocarpy, **development of fruit without fertilization of ovules.**
 
• **Female gamete undergoes development to form fruits without fertilization.**
 
• The fruit resembles a normally produced fruit but is **seedless.**
 
• Male and female gamete fertilize to form seeds, so, without fertilization the fruit is seedless.
 
 
 
• **Banana**
 
 
• Banana is** mostly propagated by rhizomes and suckers.**
 
• Banana **naturally undergoes parthenocarpy.**
 
• The produce bananas that are** sterile.**
 
• They are **without viable ovaries** and **do not produce seeds**, which means they must propagate vegetatively.
 
 
 
• **Pineapples and figs** are also examples of plants in which parthenocarpy occurs naturally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guava**

 
 
• Guava is **monoecious**, *i.e., *male and female flowers are borne on the same plant.
 
• It is a **cross pollinated** plant but in absence of bees and other pollinators,** self pollination** can also happen.
 
• Commercially guava are propagated by cuttings, air layering and grafting.
 
• Though **parthenocarpy** is possible in guava, it is **artificially induced.**
 
 
 
• **Apple**
 
 
• Apple trees are **dioecious**, which means they need **cross pollination** from another plant in order to bear fruit.
 
• Apple trees are** propagated by grafting and budding.**
 
 
 
• **Jackfruit**
 
 
• Jackfruit trees are **monoecious**, having both female and male flowers on a tree.
 
• They can **self** or **cross pollinated.**
 
• They are usually **propagated by seeds.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: External fertilization takes place in asexual reproduction
Plants have the ability to reproduce both sexually and asexually
In all viviparous organisms external fertilisation takes place

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is**__ __**__**Plants have the ability to reproduce both sexually and asexually**__

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• Reproduction is the ability of organisms to produce young ones similar to themselves.
 
• Reproduction is of two types- sexual reproduction and asexual reproduction. Sexual reproduction involves two parents
 
• whereas asexual reproduction requires a single parent and the offspring formed through asexual reproduction is like its parent. But a variation is observed in the case of sexual reproduction.

**Explanation:**__

 
• 
 
**External fertilization does not take place in asexual** reproduction: Asexual reproduction involves the production of offspring without the involvement of gametes from two parents. Therefore, external fertilization, which requires the fusion of gametes outside the parent's body, does not occur in asexual reproduction.** Statement 1 is false.**

 
 
• **Plants have the ability to reproduce both sexually and asexually,** but they have a greater capacity for asexual reproduction compared to animals.
 
• Asexual reproduction in plants can occur through various methods such as vegetative propagation, fragmentation, or budding. **Therefore, statement 2 is true.**
 
• **Viviparous organisms do not produce unfertilized eggs:** Viviparous organisms give birth to live young after internal development. The eggs in viviparous organisms are fertilized internally and undergo internal development before being born. Unfertilized eggs do not result in viable offspring.** Therefore, statement 3 is false.**
 
• **all viviparous organisms exhibit external fertilization:** Viviparous organisms give birth to live young after internal development. While many viviparous organisms do exhibit internal fertilization, where the sperm fertilizes the eggs inside the female's body, not all of them rely on external fertilization. Internal fertilization is more common in viviparous species as it provides a better chance of successful fertilization and development of the offspring. **Therefore, statement 4 is false.**

 

**Note-** ** According to the official answer key, the correct answer is Option 3.** But Viviparous organisms give birth to live offspring rather than laying eggs. They do this by fertilizing the egg inside the body, which then grows and develops inside the mother until it is born.

A common example of a viviparous organism is a mammal. Mammals (with the exceptions of monotremes like the platypus and echidna) give birth to live young.

questions.question: In plants, spore formation is a mode of reproduction that involves the production of spores. Which of the following statements about spore formation is true?

options.text: Spores are produced by flowers, and they grow into seeds.
Spores are a form of vegetative propagation in angiosperms only.
Spores are produced by non-flowering plants like ferns and mosses, and they grow into new plants.
Spores are formed through sexual reproduction in plants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spores are produced by non-flowering plants like ferns and mosses, and they grow into new plants.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Spores are primarily produced by non-flowering plants such as ferns, mosses, and fungi.
 
• Unlike seeds, spores are usually single-celled and can grow directly into a new organism without fertilization.
 
• Spores are a means of asexual reproduction, allowing plants to reproduce without the need for gamete fusion.
 
• They are adapted to survive in harsh conditions and can remain dormant until favorable growth conditions are met.
 
• When spores germinate, they develop into a new plant or organism, completing the life cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spore Definition:** A spore is a reproductive cell capable of developing into a new individual without fusion with another cell, typical of non-flowering plants, algae, fungi, and some bacteria.
 
• **Sporangium:** This is the structure where spores are produced and stored. It can be found in fungi, algae, mosses, and ferns.
 
• **Alternation of Generations:** Many plants that reproduce by spores exhibit a life cycle known as alternation of generations, which includes both a multicellular diploid phase (sporophyte) and a multicellular haploid phase (gametophyte).
 
• **Advantages of Spore Formation:** Spores are lightweight and can be dispersed by wind, water, or animals, allowing plants to colonize new environments. Their ability to remain dormant helps them survive unfavorable conditions.
 
• **Examples of Spore-Producing Plants:** Ferns, mosses, liverworts, hornworts, and fungi are common examples of organisms that reproduce through spore formation.

• In fragmentation, the cell splits into two parts and makes new bodies.

 
 
• It takes place in planaria.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/269447f0e0a9908e89c4bf617225f70e24f1dd3fa82c2e8d2de587d6ba3dc628.png] 

 
• Budding is a form of asexual reproduction in which a new individual develops from a generative anatomical point of the parent organism.

 
 
• It takes place in hydra.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c75724e780fdfbd930e11c22dae20d86af340f357e8f3e8a88277619ce9bb1c.png] 

 
• Spore Formation is a method in asexual reproduction.

 
 
• In this, a new individual is formed without fusion with another reproductive cell.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87734fc7fff01427a7e8fdde6c464e21fc4addbf691fad31b5438d493e3dd26d.png]

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement about regeneration.

options.text: These specialist cells multiply rapidly and produce a large number of new cells.
Specialised cells are responsible for regeneration.
Hydra and Planaria show regeneration mode of reproduction

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba exhibit regeneration.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Regeneration is a process whereby some organisms can regrow lost or damaged parts of their body.
 
• Specialised cells are responsible for regeneration and they multiply rapidly to form new tissues.
 
• Organisms such as Hydra and Planaria are known for their remarkable regenerative capabilities.
 
• Amoeba, being a unicellular organism, does not exhibit regeneration as it reproduces by binary fission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission:**

 
 
• A type of asexual reproduction where a single organism divides into two equal parts, each becoming a new organism.
 
• Amoeba reproduces through binary fission.
 
 
 
• **Hydra:**
 
 
• A small, freshwater organism known for its ability to regenerate entire bodies from small pieces.
 
• Regeneration occurs through the proliferation of specialized cells called interstitial cells.
 
 
 
• **Planaria:**
 
 
• A type of flatworm capable of regenerating any part of its body.
 
• Planaria utilize pluripotent stem cells known as neoblasts for regeneration.
 
 
 
• **Specialised Cells:**
 
 
• These cells have the ability to divide and differentiate to form various types of tissues and organs.
 
• They play a crucial role in the regeneration process.

**Vegetative propagation**

__
 
• Vegetative reproduction is a **form of asexual reproduction**
 
• New plant grows from a **fragment or cutting of stem, roots, leaves** of the parent plant and **specialized vegetative parts**
 
• This can occur through fragmentation and regeneration of specific vegetative parts of plants
 
• Artificial vegetative propagation is done by **cutting, grafting, layering, budding**, *etc.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The major advantage of vegetative reproduction is that the progeny is identical to the parent__
 
• New plants are produced from a single parent, *i.e., *from the vegetative part of only one individual
 
• So, the genetic material of parent and progeny is the same
 
• The progeny is a clone of parent
 
• This character is exploited commercially because desirable characters can be propagated with ease 
 
• In theory, a plant can become immortal by vegetative reproduction conserves the genetic line
 
• The same genetic material is transferred over the generation without alteration
 
• In practical, continuous cloning causes mutation, and the plant changes over time

__Hence, the correct option is option 3 - The main advantage of vegetative propagation is that is produces genetically uniform progeny.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Advantages of vegetative propagation**

 
• New plants contain genetic material of only one parent, so they are clones of the parent plant
 
• Reproduction plant with desirable traits indefinitely, preservation of characters through successive generation
 
 
• commercial production of desirable plants
 
 
 
• Bypass the immature seedling phase and therefore reach the mature phase sooner
 
 
• Lilies that normally take a few years to flower can flower within a year
 
 
 
• Quicker and more certain
 
• Plants that do not have viable seed, can be reproduced
 
 
• Seedless varieties such as banana, orange, rose, jasmine,* etc*, can be grown
 
 

**Disadvantages of vegetative reproduction**

 
• Does not produce new variety
 
• Leads to overcrowding around the parent plant
 
• Very little possibility of dispersal
 
• Success rate is very variable

questions.question: Modes of reproduction in various organisms depend on the
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**body design of the organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The mode of reproduction in organisms is significantly influenced by their **body structure and design**.
 
• Organisms with simpler body designs, such as single-celled organisms, typically reproduce asexually through processes like binary fission or budding.
 
• More complex organisms, including most animals and plants, often reproduce sexually, involving specialized reproductive organs and processes.
 
• The body design can determine the feasibility and efficiency of different reproductive strategies, ensuring the survival and adaptation of species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction**

 
 
• Involves a single parent and produces offspring identical to the parent.
 
• Common methods include binary fission, budding, fragmentation, and spore formation.
 
• Examples include bacteria (binary fission) and yeast (budding).
 
 
 
• **Sexual Reproduction**
 
 
• Involves the combination of genetic material from two parents to produce genetically diverse offspring.
 
• Involves specialized reproductive cells called gametes (sperm and egg).
 
• Common in animals, plants, and many other organisms.
 
 
 
• **Reproductive Strategies**
 
 
• Reproductive strategies can be influenced by environmental factors, availability of mates, and evolutionary pressures.
 
• Some organisms can switch between asexual and sexual reproduction based on environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation and Survival**
 
 
• Reproductive modes are crucial for the adaptation and survival of species in changing environments.
 
• Genetic diversity from sexual reproduction can enhance the resilience of populations to diseases and environmental changes.
